definition: The full recorded sequence of an agent run: thoughts, tool calls, observations, and outcome.
details: The full recorded sequence of an agent run: thoughts, tool calls, observations, and outcome. The unit of agent evaluation and of agentic RL training data; production teams collect and mine trajectories the way web teams mine logs.

explainer.lead: A trajectory is the full recorded sequence of an agent run: its thoughts, tool calls, observations, and outcome. It matters as the unit of agent evaluation and of agentic RL training data.

tiers.eli5: It's the play-by-play record of everything an AI assistant did during one task, from first thought to final answer.
tiers.practitioner: Teams collect and mine trajectories the way web teams mine logs, using them to evaluate agents and to build training data. A common pitfall is that raw trajectories are verbose and noisy, so extracting usable signal requires filtering.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, a trajectory is an ordered sequence of steps, each comprising a thought, a tool call, an observation, and eventually an outcome, recorded over one agent run. Its completeness depends on what the harness logs; missing tool outputs or truncated runs limit its use for evaluation or training.

explainer.example: An agent asked to book a flight logs its reasoning, each search and booking tool call with responses, and the final confirmation as one trajectory.
